"The company designs, supplies, installs, integrates and maintains audio-visual systems. Projects combine displays, video walls, conferencing, sound, control systems and supporting equipment for corporate, educational, hospitality and other institutional sites. Distribution sells equipment through a channel; systems integration adds design, installation and coordination; aftermarket services support installed equipment. These have different economics and should not be collapsed into a software story. [E04]

In FY2025, integration represented 58.82% of restated revenue, distribution 37.04% and aftermarket services 4.14%. Aftermarket revenue rose from ₹4.89 crore in FY2023 to only ₹5.21 crore in FY2025. The recurring-services share therefore did not drive the historical revenue surge. The offer document expressly states that the company did not manufacture the products it supplied and that supplier relationships were non-exclusive. A manufacturing facility said to have commenced in May 2026 is a later development: it cannot explain historical FY2026 production economics. [E04, E05]

Customers generally purchase projects or equipment rather than an irrevocable multiyear subscription. Cash is collected against delivery and milestones, while suppliers, inventory and installation costs often require funding first. FY2026 year-end inventory was ₹28.98 crore and receivables ₹34.25 crore. A profitable order can therefore destroy near-term liquidity even before it creates a loss. No verified cohort retention, recurring revenue reconciliation, software gross margin or customer lifetime-value data support an IP/platform valuation. [E03, E04]
